title: Lower-bound characterisation of one-way public-coin communication complexity
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function, let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, and let $m \in \bbn$. Then $m$ is a lower bound for the $\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity of $f$, in the sense that $m \le \mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon)$ as elements of $\bbn_\infty$, if and only if every protocol $p$ over a coin tape $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ of any length $n \in \bbn$ that $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ has bit cost at least $m$.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → α is a function
left side: m ≤ ε-error one-way public-coin communication complexity of f (in ℕ∞)
right side: for every n and every protocol over CoinTape(n) that ε-computes f, its cost is at least m
replaced:
For $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, and $m \in \mathbb{N}$,
the complexity satisfies $m \le \mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon)$ (as extended naturals)
if and only if every protocol $p$ over any $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ that
$\varepsilon$-computes $f$ has $p.\mathrm{cost} \ge m$.
